chunk_findings.detail: The package initializer mutates the process-wide environment (`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS`) whenever `import ddflow` is executed, not only when the ddflow CLI starts. Concrete failure: a host application imports `ddflow` to use its event log, then imports `numpy` for unrelated matrix multiplication. Because ddflow silently set the BLAS/OpenMP thread variables to `1`, the host’s unrelated numpy work is forced single-threaded, and any subprocesses spawned later inherit the cap. There is no ddflow-level opt-out except setting those environment variables before importing ddflow. This also bypasses the environment port required by [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/__init__.py:28

chunk_findings.detail: `extra_installed()` can report the rag extra as installed when it is not importable, and the result can change inside the same process. Concrete failure: put an empty `model2vec` directory on `sys.path` (a namespace package), or install a `model2vec` package that cannot import `StaticModel`. The first call to `extra_installed()` returns `True` because `find_spec("model2vec")` finds a spec. After an embedding attempt calls `_static_model()`, the import fails, `_StaticModel` is cached as `None`, and the same `extra_installed()` call now returns `False`. The previous behavior was stable (`False`) because the module-level import caught the failure. A caller that uses `extra_installed()` to choose a backend or report status gets a false positive before the first use and an inconsistent status afterward.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/embed.py:extra_installed

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test is vacuous whenever the optional `[rag]` extra/model2vec is not installed. In the unfixed code, the module-level `try: from model2vec import StaticModel` raises `ImportError` before `numpy` is imported, so the probe still prints `[]` and the assertion passes. The test never asserts that `model2vec` is actually present/importable, so in the base environment it does not fail against the unfixed code as the change promises.

chunk_findings.detail: The change still makes `import ddflow` mutate process-wide BLAS/OpenMP thread variables whenever the variables are unset. The new upgrade note states this explicitly: `import ddflow` now sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, and `MKL_NUM_THREADS` to `1` when the process has not set them. Concrete failure: a host application imports `ddflow` only to use its event log, then imports `numpy` for unrelated linear algebra. Because `ddflow` silently set `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` (and OMP/MKL) in the parent environment, the host’s unrelated numpy work is forced single-threaded for the rest of the process, and any later subprocesses inherit the cap. The cap should be limited to the CLI entry point or an explicit configurable port; a library import should not change global threading environment. This delta does not move the mutation out of the package initializer, so the previously reported side effect remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/__init__.py:28 (package initializer; confirmed by docs/ddflow/compatibility.md:152)

chunk_findings.detail: The new fake `model2vec` module still does not make the regression test bite in an environment where `numpy` is not installed. Concrete failure: run the test in the base/no-`[rag]` environment, where `numpy` is absent. The subprocess gets `PYTHONPATH=tmp_path` and `model2vec.py` containing `import numpy`. If the unfixed code still eagerly does `try: from model2vec import StaticModel` (or `try: import numpy; from model2vec import StaticModel`) at module level, the fake `model2vec` import raises `ModuleNotFoundError` on `import numpy`, the optional-dependency `try` swallows it, Python removes the failed `model2vec` module from `sys.modules`, and the probe sees neither `numpy` nor `model2vec`. The subprocess exits 0 and prints `[]`, so the assertion passes even against the unfixed eager-import code. The test needs to fake `numpy`, record the import attempt (e.g. write a sentinel file from the fake module), or otherwise guarantee it fails without the fix.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_eager_embed.py:test_cli_import_does_not_load_numpy_or_model2vec

chunk_findings.detail: The new stand-in model2vec still does not make the regression test fail against unfixed code when `numpy` itself is not installed. In the base environment without the rag extra, the old module-level `try: from model2vec import StaticModel` imports the fake file, the fake file executes `import numpy`, Python raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, and the old `ImportError` handler swallows it; Python removes the half-imported `model2vec` module from `sys.modules`, so `_PROBE` still prints `"[]"` and the assertion passes. The test must use a fake that is importable without requiring numpy (e.g. `class StaticModel: pass`), or explicitly assert numpy is available, otherwise the promised regression coverage is absent in the target environment.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_eager_embed.py:test_cli_import_does_not_load_numpy_or_model2vec

chunk_findings.detail: `extra_installed()` now calls `_static_model()`, so merely checking whether the rag extra is installed performs a real `import model2vec` and transitively imports `numpy`. A consumer that only asks `ddflow.services.embed.extra_installed()` to report availability now pays the heavy import the change exists to defer, and this directly contradicts the new documentation at `docs/ddflow/compatibility.md:156` that model2vec is imported only when an embedding is requested. The availability check should stay import-free, or the documented promise must be removed and every caller path measured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/embed.py:83

chunk_findings.detail: The new upgrade note documents—and therefore states as current behavior—that `import ddflow` sets process-wide `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, and `MKL_NUM_THREADS` to `1` when the host has not set them. A host application that imports `ddflow` to use its event log is then forced single-threaded for unrelated later numpy work, and that mutated environment is inherited by any later subprocess. The cap belongs in the CLI entrypoint, not in package import; this delta’s documentation shows the previously reported side effect still stands rather than being fixed.
